claims.statement: The canonical execution lineage is Action ≼ EPS ≼ DIC ≼ Phase ≼ Plan ≼ Goal, with package-resident identifiers and hashes.
assumptions: all canonical actions are recorded by the runtime
claims.novelty_position: engineering invariant; not claimed as a new theorem

claims.statement: Ordinary phases may progress autonomously inside an approved Plan; periodic and material events are separate governance boundaries.
Semantic refinement X ≼ Y means every trace admitted by X, after the declared abstraction map, is admitted by Y.
claims.novelty_position: standard trace-refinement formulation adapted to the hierarchy

claims.statement: For an acyclic Plan, phase contract satisfaction composes to goal satisfaction when pre/post compatibility, declared-frame noninterference, and a terminal goal implication all hold.
claims.novelty_position: known contract-composition principle; included for precision, not claimed as theorem novelty

claims.statement: Under declared read/write locality, versioned evidence, and deterministic-or-reverified phase semantics, repairing keys Δ requires invalidating only the dynamic impact cone Reach({v:R_v∩Δ≠∅}); outputs outside that cone remain contract-valid.
claims.novelty_position: adaptation of incremental-computation/build-system locality to agent workflow recovery

claims.statement: Without additional semantic information, the direct-reader seed of the dynamic impact cone is worst-case necessary: every direct reader can be made contract-invalid by some admissible phase function after Δ changes.
assumptions: phase functions may depend arbitrarily on every declared read key
claims.novelty_position: tightness characterization for the declared-footprint model

claims.statement: If the conditional probability of missing a persisting fault at each verification gate is at most α, then survival through k gates is at most α^k and the expected number of gate intervals to detection is at most 1/(1−α).
assumptions: conditional miss bound α<1 at every gate
fault remains observable at subsequent gates
claims.novelty_position: elementary reliability bound applied to evidence-gated agent execution

claims.statement: In the stated stationary cost model, checkpoint overhead U(h)=n(c_v+βc_f)/h+λnc_r h(1+α)/(2(1−α)) is minimized at h*=sqrt(2(c_v+βc_f)(1−α)/(λc_r(1+α))).
claims.novelty_position: checkpoint/restart trade-off adapted to governance cadence; not a universal prescription

claims.statement: A phase can omit global state outside its context projection without changing its action distribution only when the projection is conditionally sufficient for that phase and referenced evidence remains resolvable.
claims.novelty_position: formal condition clarifying when externalized state is safe

claims.statement: If a verifier observes a non-injective evidence map on which the goal predicate is not constant, no decision rule using only that evidence can have both zero false acceptance and zero false rejection.
assumptions: verifier decision depends only on observed evidence
claims.novelty_position: basic partial-observability impossibility; important limit, not claimed as novel in isolation

claims.statement: The relative end-to-end benefit of hierarchical execution over a flat plan increases with effective task horizon after controlling model, token budget, and tool budget.
claims.novelty_position: central empirical claim requiring confirmatory evidence

claims.statement: Verification-triggered local repair reduces downstream failure propagation and rework versus hierarchy without gated repair at matched inference budget.
The reference runtime passes its hierarchy-specific conformance tests and package recovery validation.

The defensible system contribution is the integrated object persistent intent + hierarchical refinement + bounded execution + evidence-gated verification + local repair/upward replanning, not hierarchy alone.
Hierarchical decomposition by itself guarantees correctness or preserves user intent in open-world execution.
claims.novelty_position: contradicted by observability and verifier limits

claims.statement: The current package has confirmatory evidence that it outperforms flat agents on long-horizon tasks.
